statements.action_statement: No fixed release is available yet; update when Docker Hardened Images publishes one.
statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-18477: a time-of-check to time-of-use flaw in GNU tar's handling of incremental dumpdir 'X' renames lets a local user who can write to a directory being backed up make a later restore create, rename or overwrite files outside the extraction directory, even when extracting into a new directory without -P: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-18477, https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2509735. No GNU tar release contains a fix; 1.35 is the latest release. Red Hat backported upstream GNU tar changes for it in RHSA-2026:61581 (RHEL 9) and RHSA-2026:61586 (RHEL 10). The only build of this owner published in the DHI Alpine 3.24 repository is 1.35-r5, for x86_64 and aarch64, built from Alpine's tar 1.35-r5 recipe, which builds GNU tar 1.35 with a single patch (ignore-apk-tools-checksums.patch) that does not touch this code: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/a9e2a2dc46f377eb25884f7fea9834492de7f518/main/tar/APKBUILD. Every published build is affected. Until a fix ships, avoid incremental restores (--listed-incremental or --incremental) of archives made from directories that untrusted users can write to.
